$$\int e^{iu\cdot(y+z)}\,d(\gamma_{C_1}\times\gamma_{C_2}) =\exp(-u^TC_1u/2)\exp(-u^TC_2u/2) =\exp[-u^T(C_1+C_2)u/2].$$

Since $C_1+C_2$ is positive semidefinite, [F2] and [F5] identify the pushforward under addition as $\gamma_{C_1+C_2}$. This includes singular and zero covariances.

The function $(x,y,z)\mapsto f(x+y+z)$ is nonnegative and Borel. Apply [F6] to integrate first in $y$ and then in $z$; the resulting iterated integral equals the integral against the product law of $(y,z)$. By step 1.1 its pushforward under addition is $\gamma_{C_1+C_2}$. Therefore

including the value $+\infty$. By [F1] this is exactly $T_{C_2}(T_{C_1}f)(x)=T_{C_1+C_2}f(x)$.

For finite nonnegative Borel $V$, [F1] gives $\exp[-V_{C_1}(x)]=T_{C_1}(e^{-V})(x)$ and the corresponding identity after applying $C_2$. By [A1]–[A2], the AC and Countable Choice assumptions of [F2] and [F4] hold. Apply [F2] with $m(p)=p^2$ on the sigma-finite positive-measure space $(\mathbb R,dp)$; sigma-finiteness follows from $\mathbb R=\bigcup_{n\ge1}[-n,n]$ and $[-1,1]$ has positive finite measure. It gives the self-adjoint nonnegative multiplication operator $A$ with the displayed domain and spectral calculus. The multiplier $(M^2+p^2)^{-1}$ is bounded by $M^{-2}$ and maps $H$ into $D(A)$ because $p^2/(M^2+p^2)\le1$; pointwise multiplication then shows it is the two-sided inverse of $M^2I+A$. For $u$ with bounded support, every $A^ru$ is in $H$. Pointwise finite geometric division gives
$$
(M^2+p^2)^{-1}-M^{-2}\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-p^2/M^2)^r=r_N(p^2),
$$
so the remainder on such $u$ is multiplication by $r_N(p^2)$.

The target coefficient $C_N:=M^{-2}(E^2/M^2)^{N+1}$ is finite and is strictly less than $M^{-2}$. If $N=0$, $|r_0(q)|=M^{-2}(q/M^2)/(1+q/M^2)\to M^{-2}>C_0$ as $q\to\infty$. If $N\ge1$, $|r_N(q)|=M^{-2}(q/M^2)^{N+1}/(1+q/M^2)\to\infty$. In either case choose $P>0$ so that $|r_N(p^2)|>C_N$ for every $p\in[P,P+M]$, and put $u=M^{-1/2}\mathbf1_{[P,P+M]}$. The interval has Lebesgue measure $M$, so $\|u\|_2^2=M^{-1}\int_P^{P+M}1\,dp=1$; its bounded support puts it in every $D(A^r)$, while
$$\|r_N(A)u\|_2^2=M^{-1}\int_P^{P+M}|r_N(p^2)|^2\,dp>C_N^2.$$
Thus the full-space bound fails. The restriction $E<M$ is precisely what makes the proposed low-energy coefficient smaller than the $N=0$ high-momentum limit; the example does not contradict the band-limited theorem.
